the nutritional interactions between adipose tissue and lymphoid tissue, and with how these interactions are modified by immune stimulation.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
immune stimulation prompts changes in adipose tissue that equip it to provision immune responses.
immune-stimulated proliferation of lymphoid cells in lymph nodes is fuelled by fatty acids from triacylglycerol-rich adipocytes in perinodal adipocyte depots.

the fatty acids in the triacylglyerols of the adipocytes in the perinodl adipose tissue are the main source of the fatty acids incorporated into the proliferating lymphoid cell in the activated lymph node.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

immune stimulation of a lymph node causes the local adipocytes to change the composition of their triacylglycerol stores, so as to provide a better match to the fatty acid requirements of proliferating lymphocytes in that lymph node.
the fatty acids in proliferating lymphoid cell phospholipids are derived mainly from the tri-acylglycerols (TAG) of perinodal adipocytes.
immune responses are nutritionally dependent on the fatty acids in the triacylglyerols of perinodal adipocytes, which are themselves modified by immune stimulation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
adipose tissue is not a static reservoir of energy.
the fatty acid composition in lymphoid cells is determined by that of triacylglyceroles in the perinodally located adipocytes.
adipose depots are not just storage depots but are specialized depots with specific functions.
